atAGlance: Súp cua is a thick crab soup with egg ribbons, pepper, cilantro, and sometimes corn or asparagus. It is warm, silky, and snack-sized.
whatItIs: Súp cua is thick crab soup with egg ribbons, crab meat, mushrooms or quail egg, cilantro, and black pepper. It is silky, warming, and often sold as a small snack bowl.
howToEnjoy: Stir gently, add pepper or chili oil only after tasting, and eat while hot so the egg ribbons and crab stay silky.
howLocalsOrder: Order súp cua by bowl size, then ask for no pepper or no chili oil if you want it gentle. Ask about crab or quail egg if allergies matter.
worthKnowing: This is a comfort snack rather than a seafood feast; the texture should be thick and spoonable.
goodToKnow: A little pepper or chili can wake up the bowl, but the texture should stay silky and crab-sweet.
travelerCaution: Contains or may contain seafood or shellfish.
